$comment: VANISH BROKER REGISTRY — static, version-controlled reference data (PRD §16).
This is NOT user data. Adding coverage = adding a record, no code change.
PRIMARY SOURCE: California Privacy Protection Agency Data Broker Registry.
https://cppa.ca.gov/data_broker_registry/complete-reg-data-brokers.csv
Pulled 2026-08-06. 549 registered brokers.
Why this source and not the brokers' own marketing pages: under California's
Delete Act (SB 362) a data broker doing business in California MUST register
annually with the CPPA and disclose how consumers opt out. That filing is a
legal declaration, not marketing copy, and it is published as machine-readable
CSV. It is more authoritative than a footer link that can be reworded or moved,
and it is reachable without fighting anyone's bot detection.
It also corrected two records that had been taken from the brokers' own pages:
BeenVerified's CCPA contact is ccpa@ (not privacy@), and Spokeo publishes a
dedicated CCPA phone line. Prefer the registry when the two disagree.
VERIFICATION RULE: never enable a broker whose optOutUrl / emailTo has not been
read off an authoritative source. A wrong opt-out address means the user's
removal request goes nowhere while they believe they are protected — that is
worse than not listing the broker at all.
scanStrategy:
'html-parse' — the broker serves its public search results to a plain request.
'assisted'   — the broker blocks automated requests (HTTP 403). Vanish does NOT
attempt to defeat that. The user opens the search link in their
own browser, confirms whether they are listed, and pastes the
listing URL back. Verified per broker on 2026-08-06.
NOT INCLUDED — Radaris and TruePeopleSearch. Both are plainly people-search data
brokers, but neither appears anywhere in the California registry under any name.
With no state filing and no reachable page, there is no authoritative opt-out
address to give a user, so they are omitted rather than guessed at.

brokers.name: Spokeo
brokers.note: Paste the exact profile URL and your email, then click the link Spokeo emails you — the removal does not take effect until you do. Each listing must be opted out separately. Spokeo's CCPA rights portal is at spokeo.com/privacy/control, and they take CCPA requests by phone.

brokers.name: BeenVerified
brokers.note: One opt-out here also covers their sister sites — PeopleLooker, NeighborWho and NumberGuru are the same company. Their privacy policy §19.6 expressly accepts authorized-agent requests.

brokers.name: Whitepages
brokers.note: Whitepages has historically asked for phone verification to complete a suppression. Their CCPA filing doesn't mention it, so it may have changed — if they ask, it's them, not a phishing step.

brokers.name: TruthFinder
brokers.note: Reachable from their homepage as "Do Not Sell My Personal Information" or "Suppress My Data" if the direct link moves.

brokers.name: Instant Checkmate
brokers.note: Same operator as TruthFinder — opting out of one does not opt you out of the other. Do both.

brokers.name: PeopleSearcher
brokers.note: Also reachable from their homepage as "Do Not Sell My Info". Their search page returns a JavaScript shell with no server-rendered text, so Vanish can't read it — see docs/SCAN-VIABILITY.md.

brokers.name: Intelius
brokers.note: Intelius also runs US Search. Their site route means finding your profile and using the "Do Not Sell My Personal Information" link at the bottom of the page; the email below is the route they filed with California, so it works without hunting for the link.

brokers.name: Nuwber
brokers.note: Email is the only opt-out route Nuwber filed — there is no form. Send the message below and keep the sent copy.

brokers.name: PeopleFinders
brokers.note: PeopleFinders didn't file a direct opt-out URL — you reach it from the "Do Not Sell My Info" link in their site footer, or from Section V of the privacy policy linked here.
